26-1102132011.title: Certified Public Accountant, Licensed
26-1102132011.description: An applicant for a Michigan Certified Public Accountant (CPA) License must complete 150 semester-hours of college education, including a Bachelor's degree or higher with a concentration in Accounting. Upon meeting this requirement, the required CPA exam must be taken and passed. Finally, after 2,000 hours of qualifying experience has been attained, a licensing application can be submitted along with a $300 application fee to the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs.
26-1102132011.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-8600392010.title: Horse Racing Occupational License
26-8600392010.description: To receive a Horse Racing Occupational License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must be familiar with Michigan laws and regulations governing pari-mutuel horse racing in the state, access and complete the license application, sign and either hand deliver or mail the application the to Michigan Gaming Control Board and remit the appropriate fee.
26-8600392010.agency: Michigan Department of Agriculture and Rural Development

00-78.title: Enrolled Actuary
00-78.description: Enrolled Actuaries meet experience requirements and pass an examination. EAs are experts on the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA). The EA designation is awarded by the Joint Board for the Enrollment of Actuaries, located at the Internal Revenue Service, U.S. Department of the Treasury. Renewal every 3 years requires continuing actuarial education and other professional development activities. For detailed information, see http://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-utl/20cfr901.pdf or http://www.irs.gov/taxpros/actuaries/index.html.
00-78.agency: U.S. Department of the Treasury · Joint Board for the Enrollment of Actuaries

26-6200172199.title: Engineer, Licensed Professional
26-6200172199.description: To receive a Professional Engineers License from the State of Michigan, an applicant must attain a bachelor's or master's degree from a an accredited school and program and possess four years or more of acceptable engineering work experience AFTER having received a bachelor's degree. Additionally, an applicant must pass the Fundamentals of Engineering NCEES examination ($225 cost) as well as the Principles of Engineering NCEES examination ($350). Upon completion of these requirements, an applicant must submit an online license application along with the $75.00 application fee.
26-6200172199.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2380050391.title: Stationary Engineer
26-2380050391.description: To receive a Stationary Engineer license, an applicant must submit a completed Stationary Engineer Examination application, required documents, and license fee ($80.00). Additionally, the Stationary Engineer Examination must be completed and passed.
26-2380050391.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

00-18.title: Air Traffic Control Tower Operator
00-18.description: Requirements to obtain an Air Traffic Control Tower Operator certificate include passing a written test. Besides the basic certificate, to act at any operating position, the individual must pass a practical test on control tower equipment and its use. To obtain a facility rating, the individual must have at least six months experience and pass another practical test. This certificate is valid until surrendered, suspended or revoked, although the individual must maintain current experience to work under the certificate. Detailed information can be found at web sites:http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ, http://www.natca.org/assets/Documents/mediacenter/controller_brochure.pdf, http://www2.faa.gov/careers/employment/atc.htm, and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.31-65.50.

00-12.title: Aircraft Mechanic - A & P
00-12.description: Aircraft mechanics are certified by the FAA with either an airframe (A) or powerplant (P) rating. Initial ratings require either completion of FAA Approved Aviation Maintenance Technician School or 18 months of work experience. Applicants must pass written, oral and practical exams. Thirty months of work experience is required for a combined Airframe & Powerplant (A & P) certificate. To obtain an inspector's authorization, a mechanic must have held an A & P certificate for at least 3 years. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked, but requires currency of experience or refresher training. For further information, go the web site of the Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS): http://umet-vets.dol.gov/airframe-mechanic.htm, http://www1.faa.gov/AVR/afs/mechanics.htm, and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.71-65.95.

00-16.title: Aircraft Repairer
00-16.description: To be eligible for a repairman certificate, a person must have the qualifications needed on the job. These qualifications may be obtained through 18 months of work experience or completion of formal training. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www2.faa.gov/education/rlib/career.htm and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.101-65.105.

00-02.title: Airline Transport Pilot
00-02.description: To become certified (licensed) as an Airline Transport Pilot (ATP), an individual must have a Commercial Pilot certificate or equivalent with an instrument rating for airplane, helicopter, or powered-lift (glider). Air flight training and ground school as well as flight experience are requirements. They also must pass a strict physical examination and have 20/20 vision with or without glasses, good hearing, and no physical handicaps that could impair performance. They must pass a written test and a demonstration of flying ability. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.151-61.167.

00-08.title: Commercial Pilot
00-08.description: All pilots who are paid to transport passengers or cargo must have a Commercial Pilot's license with an instrument rating issued by the FAA. To qualify for this license, the applicant must be at least 18 years old and have at least 250 hours of flight experience. The time can be reduced through participation in certain flight school curricula approved by the FAA. The individual also must pass a strict physical examination and have 20/20 vision with or without glasses, good hearing, and no physical handicaps that could impair performance. Passing a written test and a demonstration of flying ability are required. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.121-61.133 and http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf.

00-15.title: Flight Engineer
00-15.description: To become certified as a Flight Engineer requires that the individual have either training or experience. Passing a written exam and a practical test and having a current medical certificate are also required. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://umet-vets.dol.gov/flightengineer.htm and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr63_00.html, parts 63.31-63.43.

00-77.title: Flight Instructor
00-77.description: To obtain certification as a Flight Instructor, the individual must hold either a Commercial Pilot or Airline Transport Pilot certificate with appropriate aircraft and instrument ratings. Training is required as well as experience in the type of aircraft being rated. This license is valid for 2 years and may be renewed by one of several options, such as passing a practical test, documenting student success, or taking a refresher course. More details can be found at web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.181-61.199, www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf, and http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ.

00-20.title: Flight Navigator
00-20.description: To become certified as a Flight Navigator, the individual must be at least 21 years old and have a medical certificate. He or she must have both training in flight navigation and practical experience. Passing written and practical tests are required as well as having a current medical certificate. This certificate is valid until surrendered, suspended, or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web site: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr63_00.html, parts 63.51-63.61.

00-13.title: Ground Instructor
00-13.description: To obtain certification as a Ground Instructor, the individual must pass an aircraft navigation knowledge test and a test of the fundamentals of instructing, unless the person already is employed as a teacher or holds a teacher's certification. Detailed information can be found at web sites: http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.211-61.217.

requirements.label: Certification
requirements.value: Certification my substitute for license requirements

00-06.title: Private Pilot
00-06.description: Obtaining a Private Pilot certificate (license) requires the individual to complete ground and flight training, have flight experience, obtain a medical certificate, and pass a written exam as well as a demonstration of flying ability. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. The FAA Advisory Circular, AC 61-12M, Student Pilot Guide, outlines general procedures for obtaining student and private pilot certificates. Detailed information can be found at web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.102-61.117, and http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf.

26-7501492098.title: Fire Alarm Contractor
26-7501492098.description: To receive a Fire Alarm Contractor License, an applicant must hold a Fire Alarm Specialty Technician's License OR must have at least 1 fire alarm specialty technician residing in Michigan who is employed by the applicant full-time. Additionally, an applicant must take and pass the Electrical/Farm Alarm/Sign Contractor exam and submit the $300.00 license fee.
26-7501492098.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-7503492098.title: Fire Alarm Specialty Apprentice Technician
26-7503492098.description: To receive a Fire Alarm Specialty Apprentice Technician license in the State of Michigan, an applicant must submit an application online or mail the completed application and required documents to the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs. Additionally, they must remit the $15.00 application fee.

requirements.label: Certification
requirements.value: Certification my substitute for license requirements

26-7503492098.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-7502492098.title: Fire Alarm Specialty Technician
26-7502492098.description: An applicant for a Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License in the State of Michigan must be at least 20 years old, have received a certification by the National Institute for Certification in Engineering Technology as an engineering technician, level 2, or equivalent level, and must take and pass the Fire Alarm Specialty Technician examination. The license application fee is $50.00.

requirements.label: Certification
requirements.value: Certification my substitute for license requirements

26-7502492098.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-3600492098.title: Security Alarm Contractor
26-3600492098.description: A security alarm system contractor must post a $25,000 surety bond with the Department or furnish an insurance policy in the amount of $25,000 for property damages, $100,000 for injury or death of one person, and $200,000 for injuries to or deaths of more than one person. In addition, a candidate must have the correct combination of work experience or take the exam. The fee for this license is $500.00.
26-3600492098.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Corporations, Securities & Commercial

26-3201533011.title: Medical First Responder
26-3201533011.description: Medical first responders must take an initial education course, register nationally, and pass the cognitive exam. There is no fee for this license.
26-3201533011.agency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services · Emergency Medical Services

00-60.title: Medical Doctor
00-60.description: A ship's Medical Doctor is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A medical doctor must also hold a valid license as a physician or surgeon issued within the United States. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-60.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

26-4305291060.title: Medical Doctor (M.D.)
26-4305291060.description: A medical doctor must be a graduate from an approved medical school, complete two years of accredited postgraduate training and pass the U.S. Medical Licensure Examination. The fee for this license is $302.25 and a license must be renewed on a three year cycle.
26-4305291060.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-4301291060.title: Medical Doctor, Clinical Academic (M.D.)
26-4301291060.description: A clinical academic medical doctor must be a graduate of an approved medical school and be appointed to a teaching or research position in Michigan. A renewal fee of $31.80 must be paid annually.
26-4301291060.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-4303291060.title: Medical Doctor, Educational Limited (M.D.)
26-4303291060.description: A medical doctor intern must be a graduate from an approved medical school and appointed to a postgraduate training program in Michigan. The renewal fee for this license $31.80 annually.
26-4303291060.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-5100291060.title: Osteopathic Physician (D.O.)
26-5100291060.description: An osteopathic physician must be a graduate of an approved program, pass the national examination, and complete 1 year of post graduate training. The fee for this license is $159.05.
26-5100291060.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-1300171011.title: Architects
26-1300171011.description: To receive a Michigan Architects License, an applicant must have completed an approved internship program, attained a degree in architecture, and complete the Architect Registration Examination. Additionally, an online license application should be submitted along with the $65.00 application fee.
26-1300171011.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

00-48.title: Second Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-48.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Second Assistant Engineer - Upper Level, the applicant must, while holding a license as a Third Assistant Engineer, complete one of the following: 360 days of service as an Assistant Engineer; or a minimum of 180 days as an Assistant Engineer and 360 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED); or 360 days as Chief Engineer (Limited-Oceans). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-48.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-38.title: Second Mate - Upper Level
00-38.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Second Mate Upper Level requires 360 days service as Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch (OIC) on ocean steam or motor vessels while licensed as a Third Mate. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Detailed information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-38.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

26-1502272021.title: Boxer
26-1502272021.description: To renew the Professional Boxer License, an individual must submit a license renewal fee of $45.00.
26-1502272021.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Corporations, Securities & Commercial

26-3000299091.title: Athletic Trainer
26-3000299091.description: To receive a Michigan Athletic Trainer License, an applicant must undergo a fingerprint and criminal background check and complete training to identify victims of human trafficking. Additionally, an applicant must complete a minimum of 1 hour of first aid training with the 3 years prior to the application date, attain certification in emergency cardiac care, complete the Board of Certification, Inc. examination, and submit a license application with the appropriate fee remitted.
26-3000299091.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-1600291121.title: Audiologist
26-1600291121.description: To obtain an Audiology License, an applicant must hold the equivalent of a U.S. master's or doctoral degree in audiology. Those without a doctor of audiology degree must complete at least 9 months (1,260 hours) of supervised clinical experience in audiology. Additionally, an applicant must submit a license application with fee ($286.40), undergo a fingerprint/criminal background check, and pass the PRAXIS exam. Licenses must be renewed every 2 years.
26-1600291121.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

00-65.title: Ship Radar Endorsement
00-65.description: The Ship Radar Endorsement is issued by the Federal Communications Commission to licensed commercial radio operators. This endorsement allows them to repair, maintain, or internally adjust ship radar equipment. Passing a written exam is required. For further information, see the FCC web site at http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/sre.html.

26-1700395011.title: Barber
26-1700395011.description: To receive a Barber's License, an applicant must beat at least 17 years old, have completed the equivalent of a 10th grade education, complete at least 1,800 hours at a licensed barber college, and pass the theory and practical examination administered by PSI Services, LLC. The license application fee is $20.00, with an annual renewal fee of $30.00.
26-1700395011.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-1702251194.title: Barber Instructor
26-1702251194.description: To receive a Barber Instructor License, an applicant must first have attained the equivalent of a high school diploma. Beyond high school, an applicant must have attended a licensed barber college with 1 year of instruction completed, OR have completed 60 semester hours in an approved course with 6 months of instruction in barbering. Finally, a theory exam administered by PSI Services, LLC must be passed, and a license application with $20.00 fee submitted to the Department of Licensing and Regulatory affairs. The annual renewal fee is $40.00.
26-1702251194.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-1703395011.title: Barber Student
26-1703395011.description: To receive a Barber Student License, an applicant must have an education equivalent to completing the 10th grade. They must also submit a license application along with the appropriate licensing fee ($80.00).
26-1703395011.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2205627927.title: Barber Student Instructor
26-2205627927.description: To receive a Barber Student Instructor license, an applicant must have received a high school diploma or equivalent, and must be a licensed barber with at least 2 years of experience.
26-2205627927.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-5365420611.title: Natural Hair Culturist Limited Instructor
26-5365420611.description: To receive a Natural Hair Culturist Limited Instructor License in Michigan, an applicant must first have attained a high school diploma or its equivalent, have completed at least 300 hours of instructor training and have passed the theory and practical exam administered by PSI Services. Upon completion of these requirements, an applicant can then submit an Instructor License application along with the appropriate fee ($63.00).
26-5365420611.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2700395012.title: Cosmetologist
26-2700395012.description: To receive a Cosmetology License in Michigan, an applicant must be at least 17 years old, have attained the educational equivalent of 9th grade, and have completed at least 1,500 of cosmetology training OR performed a 2-year cosmetology apprenticeship. Upon meeting these requirements, they must pass the required exam administered by PSI Services and submit a license application along with the accompanying application fee.
26-2700395012.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2716395012.title: Cosmetologist, Apprentice
26-2716395012.description: To receive a Cosmetology Apprentice License, an applicant must submit a registration application the Michigan Bureau of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs and remit the $25.00 application fee.
26-2716395012.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2701251194.title: Cosmetology Instructor
26-2701251194.description: To receive a Cosmetology Instructor License in Michigan, an applicant must have attained a high school diploma or its equivalent, have a current Michigan cosmetology license, and have at least 3 years of practical experience in natural hair cultivation, hair service, skin care services, and manicuring services (which includes 1 year in a cosmetology establishment). Finally, the applicant must have at least 500 hours of instructor training, and must pass the theory and practical examination administered by PSI Services. Upon completion of these requirements, an applicant can then submit an Instructor License application along with the appropriate fee.
26-2701251194.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2702251194.title: Cosmetology, Limited Instructor
26-2702251194.description: To receive a Cosmetology Limited Instructor's License in Michigan, an applicant must have attained a high school diploma or its equivalent, have a current Michigan cosmetology license, and have completed at least 500 hours of instructor training. Finally the theory and practical examination administered by PSI Services must be passed. Upon completion of these requirements, an applicant can then submit an Instructor License application along with the appropriate fee ($63.00).
26-2702251194.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2707395012.title: Electrologist
26-2707395012.description: To receive an Electrologist License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must be at least 18 years old, have attained the educational equivalent of 9th grade, and have completed at least 400 hours of cosmetology training OR performed a 6-month cosmetology apprenticeship. Upon meeting these requirements, they must pass the required theory and practical exam administered by PSI Services and submit a license application along with the accompanying application fee.
26-2707395012.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2725251194.title: Electrologist Instructor
26-2725251194.description: To receive an Electrology Instructor License in Michigan, an applicant must have attained a high school diploma or its equivalent, have a current Michigan electrologist license, and have at least 3 years of practical experience in electrology (which includes 1 year in a cosmetology establishment holding a limited license for the practice of electrologist). Finally, the applicant must have at least 300 hours of instructor training, and must pass the theory and practical examination administered by PSI Services. Upon completion of these requirements, an applicant can then submit an Instructor License application along with the appropriate fee ($63.00).
26-2725251194.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-6420327267.title: Electrologist Limited Instructor
26-6420327267.description: To receive an Electrologist Limited Instructor license, an applicant must have at least a high school diploma or equivalent level of education, have a current Michigan electrologist license, must have completed at least 300 hours of instructor training, and must have passed the theory and practical examination administered by PSI. Upon meeting these requirements, a licensure application along with the appropriate fee ($63.00) should be submitted to the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory affairs.
26-6420327267.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2717395012.title: Electrologist, Apprentice
26-2717395012.description: To receive an Electrologist Apprentice License, an applicant must submit a registration application the Michigan Bureau of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs and remit the $25.00 application fee.
26-2717395012.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2714395012.title: Natural Hair Culturist
26-2714395012.description: A manicurist must complete not less than 400 hours of training in a licensed school of cosmetology or perform a 6-month apprenticeship program within a licensed cosmetology establishment. A manicurist must pass the required theory and practical examination administered by PSI Services, LLC (PSI). Licenses expire biennially, the renewal fee is $48.00.
26-2714395012.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2723251194.title: Natural Hair Culturist Instructor
26-2723251194.description: A natural hair culturist instructor must hold a current Michigan license, have at least 3 years of practical experience, and completed 300 hours of instructor training. Licenses expire biennially, the renewal fee is $48.00.
26-2723251194.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2720395012.title: Natural Hair Culturist, Apprentice
26-2720395012.description: An apprentice must be under the supervision of a license holder and pay the registration of $25.00.
26-2720395012.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-8503391020.title: Casino Employees Level 3
26-8503391020.description: An applicant for a Casino Level 3 License must first apply to the casino's or supplier's Human Resources Department, who must provide a written statement that the casino/supplier has hired or intends to hire the applicant. An application along with a $50 application fee must be submitted to the Michigan Gaming and Control Board. Finally, a background examination must be completed and a $50 license fee submitted.

26-6319287916.title: Certified Peer Recovery Mentor (C.P.R.M.)
26-6319287916.description: To receive a Certified Peer Recovery Mentor certification, an applicant must first acquire up to 500 hours of full or part-time alcohol or drug addiction peer recovery support services. Additionally, they must have a high school diploma or equivalency and up to 46 education hours of education in Peer Recovery support within the areas defined by the IC&RC Peer Recovery Performance domains. Furthermore, an applicant must have 25 hours or more of direct supervision performing peer recovery mentor functions, with at least 5 hours in each domain. Finally, once these qualifications have been met, the IC&RC/PR exam must be taken and passed and a licensing application submitted to the Michigan Certification Board for Addiction Professionals. The accompanying application fee is $65.00.
26-6319287916.agency: Michigan Certification Board for Addiction Professionals

26-2401431011.title: Collection Agency Manager
26-2401431011.description: An applicant for a Collection Agency Manager License must be at least 18 years old, have a high school diploma or equivalent level of education, and complete at least 6 months of full-time experience in account collection. Upon completing these requirements , the required exam administered by PSI Services, LLC must be passed (exam fee is $56.00). Finally, an application along with appropriate fee should be submitted to the Michigan Bureau of Licensing and Regulatory affairs. The application fee is $85.00 for non-owner managers OR no fee for owner managers.
26-2401431011.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

00-21.title: FIRST Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T1
00-21.description: FIRST Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T1) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. Further information can be found at the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-24.title: General Radiotelephone Operator License - PG
00-24.description: General Radiotelephone Operator License (PG) is issued for a lifetime and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-26.title: GMDSS Radio Maintainer's License - DM
00-26.description: GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) Radio Maintainer's License (DM) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-27.title: GMDSS Radio Operator's License - DO
00-27.description: GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) Radio Operator's License (DO) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-25.title: Marine Radio Operator Permit - MP
00-25.description: Marine Radio Operator Permit (MP) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-58.title: Radio Officer
00-58.description: The Radio Officer's license is issued to applicants who have a valid Federal Communications Commission (FCC) license as first or second class radiotelegraph operator (T1, T2). Certain officers are required to hold Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS) certification issued by the FCC. Further information can be found at theUSCG website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-58.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-75.title: Restricted Radiotelephone Operator Permit (RP)
00-75.description: RP holders are authorized to operate most aircraft and aeronautical ground stations. They can also operate marine radiotelephone stations aboard pleasure craft (other than those carrying more than six passengers for hire on the Great Lakes or bays or tidewaters or in the open sea) when operator licensing is required. To obtain this permit, you must be able to speak and hear; and keep a written log; and be familiar with provisions of applicable treaties, laws and rules which govern the radio station you will operate. For further information, see the Federal Communications web site at http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/rp.html.

00-22.title: SECOND Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T2
00-22.description: SECOND Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T2) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-23.title: THIRD Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T3
00-23.description: THIRD Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T3) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-57.title: Assistant Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels
00-57.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as an Assistant Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels include 1,080 days at sea with 720 days on Motor Vessels. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-57.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-56.title: Chief Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels
00-56.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels include 1,440 days at sea with 360 days as a Licensed Engineer and 950 days on Motor Vessels. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm.
00-56.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-19.title: Inspector's Authorization
00-19.description: To obtain an inspector's authorization, a mechanic must have held an Aircraft Mechanic A & P certificate for at least 3 years. For further information, see web site http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ, parts 65.91-65.95.

00-41.title: Operator of Uninspected Passenger Vessels - OUPV
00-41.description: To become licensed as an Operator of Uninspected Passenger Vessels requires specific experience -- Near Coastal or Inland as well as passing a written exam. Recent training in First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is also required. For complete details see the USCG web page http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr13_02, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at website http://frwebgate4.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/waisgate.cgi?WAISdocID=50846230377+3+0+0&WAISaction=retrieve or http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-41.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-42.title: Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels - OUTV
00-42.description: To become licensed as a an Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels (OUTV) or 2nd Class Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels (OUTV) requires specific experience - Oceans (Domestic Route), Near Coastal or Inland, as well as passing a written exam. Recent training in First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is also required. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Details can be found on the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-42.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

26-8004452011.title: Certified Field Person
26-8004452011.description: To receive a Certified Field person License, an individual must work with a dairy inspector on 25 farms and agree within 80% of those farm inspections. Additionally, an application along with a $150 application fee must be submitted to the Michigan Department of Agriculture.
26-8004452011.agency: Michigan Department of Agriculture and Rural Development

26-7001474011.title: Inspector, Building
26-7001474011.description: To receive a Building Inspector License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must have four years of experience actively engaged in the construction business, must possess a license as an architect or engineer with the State of Michigan, and must have either an Associates or Bachelor's degree in a construction-related field. Upon meeting these requirements, an applicant must submit a license application along with the appropriate application fee ($25.00 per classification).
26-7001474011.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-7004474011.title: Inspector, Mechanical
26-7004474011.description: To receive a Mechanical Inspector License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must have a minimum of three years of experience in hydronic heating and cooling and process piping, HVAC equipment, ductwork, refrigeration, limited heating service, unlimited heating service, limited refrigeration and air conditioning service, unlimited refrigeration and air condition service, and fire suppression. They must also obtain a specialty license if applicable. Upon meeting these requirements, an applicant must also take and pass an examination for each work classification desired. To do so, they must submit of a license application to the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs, along with the $300.00 license and application fee.
26-7004474011.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-8842533041.title: Chauffeur License
26-8842533041.description: An applicant for the Chauffeur License must be at least 16 years old, have completed driver education, and passed a chauffeur license knowledge test. Once these requirements have been met, a $35 license fee must be submitted to the Secretary of State.

26-cdl.title: Commercial Drivers License (CDL)
26-cdl.description: Commercial Drivers Licenses are issued by state departments but are similar from state to state, since the minimum requirements of the licenses and endorsements are set centrally. For more information contact the state DMV or https://cms.fmcsa.dot.gov/registration/commercial-drivers-license/how-do-i-get-commercial-drivers-license.

26-5103291060.title: Osteopathic Physician, Educational Limited (D.O.)
26-5103291060.description: An osteopathic physician intern must be a graduate of an approved program and complete a certification of appointment. The fee for this license is $180.25.
26-5103291060.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2100119021.title: Residential Builder
26-2100119021.description: A residential builder must have 60 hours of approved prelicensure education prior to taking the licensure exam. The fee for this license is $195.00.
26-2100119021.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-8293807356.title: Family/Group Child Care Home
26-8293807356.description: To receive a Family Child Care Home license, an applicant must read the Licensing Rules for Family and Group Child Care Homes, as well as the Child Care Organizations Act. After meeting these requirements, the online application must be submitted along with the $50.00 application fee.
26-8293807356.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Community and Health Systems

26-2300291011.title: Chiropractic
26-2300291011.description: To apply for a Michigan Chiropractic License, an individual must first graduate from a chiropractic educational program that has been accredited by the Council on Chiropractic Education. Once this has been completed, Parts 1, 2, 3, and 4 of the National Board of Chiropractic Examiners examination must be passed. Finally, a licensure application along with the appropriate fee ($53 to $127.25) should be submitted to the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs, and a fingerprint report and background check completed.
26-2300291011.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-1872355127.title: Chiropractic - Educational Limited
26-1872355127.description: To apply for a Michigan Chiropractic Educational Limited License, an individual must complete at least two years, four semesters, or six quarter terms in a chiropractic school that has been accredited by the Council on Chiropractic Education. An applicant must also have arranged for supervision from a Michigan-licensed Chiropractor for the 6-months duration of a the chiropractic education. Once this has been completed, a license application along with the appropriate application fee ($53.00) must be submitted, and a fingerprint report and background check completed.
26-1872355127.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-8904131031.title: Adjuster for the Insured (Public Adjuster)
26-8904131031.description: An applicant for the Adjuster for the Insured License must first file an Electronic Resident Licensing application via the National Producer License Registry website. The application and license fee is $15.00, plus a $5.00 transaction fee. Additionally, an applicant must complete a Michigan licensing examination.
26-8904131031.agency: Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services

26-8903131031.title: Insurance Adjuster (Independent Adjuster)
26-8903131031.description: To receive an Insurance Adjuster (Independent Adjuster) License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must complete the examination and file an Electronic Resident Licensing application through the National Producer License Registry website. The license application fee is $15.00 plus a $5.00 transaction fee.
26-8903131031.agency: Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services

26-8901413021.title: Insurance Agent (Insurance Producer)
26-8901413021.description: To receive an Insurance Agent (Insurance Producer) License in the State of Michigan, an applicant needs to be at least 18 years of age and have completed the required pre-licensing education. The pre-licensing education consists of completing an approve 20-hour classroom course or an approved self-study course, and taking the corresponding examination within 12 months of course completion. Finally, an applicant must successfully complete the Michigan licensing examination. Once these requirements have been met, an applicant must file an Electronic Resident Licensing (ERL) application through the National Insurance Producer Registry website, along with the $10.00 application fee and $5.00 transaction fee.
26-8901413021.agency: Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services

26-8902413021.title: Insurance Agent, Surplus Lines
26-8902413021.description: To receive a Resident Surplus Lines Producer License, an applicant must have successfully completed the Surplus Lines examination. Upon meeting this requirement, they must file an Electronic Resident Licensing application through the National Insurance Producer Registry website and remit the $110.00 license fee and $5.00 transaction fee.
26-8902413021.agency: Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services

26-8905413021.title: Insurance Counselor
26-8905413021.description: To receive an Insurance Counselor License from the State of Michigan, an applicant must have successfully completed the required examination. Upon meeting this requirement, they must file an Electronic Resident Licensing application through the National Insurance Producer Registry website and remit the $20.00 license fee and $5.00 transaction fee.
26-8905413021.agency: Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services

26-8907413021.title: Insurance Solicitor
26-8907413021.description: To receive an Insurance Solicitor License from the State of Michigan, an applicant must have successfully completed the required pre-licensing education coursework and passed the required examination. Upon meeting these requirements, they must file an Electronic Resident Licensing application through the National Insurance Producer Registry website and remit the $20.00 license fee and $5.00 transaction fee.
26-8907413021.agency: Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services

26-8113131021.title: Fur Dealer
26-8113131021.description: A fur dealer must apply for a permit with the Department of Natural Resources.

26-8143453011.title: Minnow, Wiggler & Crayfish Dealer
26-8143453011.description: A license must be obtained from Michigan Department of Natural Resources for Minnow, Wiggler, & Crayfish Dealers. The fee is $25.00.

26-8001453011.title: Wholesale Fish Dealer
26-8001453011.description: Any person engaged in wholesale of fish must apply for license with the Department of Natural Resources. The Licensees must submit monthly reports to the Department of Natural Resources. The fee for this license is $5.00.

26-7702474011.title: Asbestos Abatement Inspector
26-7702474011.description: To receive an Asbestos Abatement Inspector License, an applicant must have worked at least one year in asbestos-related work or general building inspections that are related to environmental and health concerns, OR have at least five years of supervisory experience in general building operations and maintenance. Additionally, an applicant must receive Michigan or EPA-approved training and receive accreditation from MIOSHA Asbestos Program. The fee schedule for accreditation is $150.00.
26-7702474011.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Occupational Safety & Health Administration

26-7706192041.title: Asbestos Management Planner
26-7706192041.description: To receive an Asbestos Management Planner License, an applicant must have had at least two years of experience in Asbestos-related work, OR have had at least five years of experience in school building operations and maintenance. Additionally, an applicant must receive Michigan or EPA-approved training and receive accreditation from MIOSHA Asbestos Program. The fee schedule for accreditation is $150.00.
26-7706192041.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Occupational Safety & Health Administration

26-2102119021.title: Residential Maintenance and Alteration Contractor
26-2102119021.description: A maintenance and alteration contractor must have 60 hours of approved prelicensure education prior to taking the licensure exam. The fee for this license is $195.00.
26-2102119021.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-7601119021.title: Sign Specialty Contractor
26-7601119021.description: A sign contractor must hold a sign specialist license and provide proof of public liability insurance. The fee for this license is $200.00
26-7601119021.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-1171190934.title: Certified Stenographic Reporter (C.S.R.)
26-1171190934.description: To receive certification as a Certified Stenographic Reporter, an individual must have successfully completed an approved, accredited, or recognized course of study in court reporting, and must also pass the registered professional reporter skills examination. Additionally, an applicant must pass the CSR written examination. Upon meeting these qualifications, an applicant must submit an application for certification.

26-1470008364.title: Certified Stenomask Reporter (C.S.M.R.)
26-1470008364.description: To receive certification as a Certified Stenomask Reporter, an individual must have successfully completed an approved, accredited, or recognized course of study in court reporting, which can be found on the National Verbatim Reporters Association website. Additionally, the applicant must pass the certified verbatim reporter skills examination as well as the CSMR examination. Upon meeting these requirements, an applicant must submit an application for certification.

26-8701252021.title: School Teacher, Elementary & Secondary
26-8701252021.description: School Teachers must be graduates of approved education programs, complete reading courses, first aid training, and pass the basic skills examination and the certification examination. The fee for this license is $160.00.

26-4662179393.title: Dental Assistant, Clinical/Nonclinical Limited (R.D.A.)
26-4662179393.description: To receive an RDA Clinical/Nonclinical Limited License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must graduate from a CODA/ADA-accredited dental assisting program, must be enrolled in a postgraduate educational program, and take and pass a fingerprint report and criminal background check. After meeting these requirements, the applicant must submit a license application along with the appropriate fee ($21.20).
26-4662179393.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-4662179399.title: Dental Assistant, Educational Limited (R.D.A.)
26-4662179399.description: To receive an RDA Educational Limited License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must graduate from a CODA/ADA-accredited dental assisting program, must be enrolled in a postgraduate educational program, and take and pass a fingerprint report and criminal background check. After meeting these requirements, the applicant must submit a license application along with the appropriate fee ($21.20).
26-4662179399.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2918319091.title: Dental Assistant, Registered (R.D.A.)
26-2918319091.description: To receive a Registered Dental Assistant License, an applicant must graduate from a CODA/ADA-accredited dental assisting program, have competency in applying and removing a dental dam, and pass the Michigan Clinical and Written RDA Examination. After meeting these requirements, the applicant must submit a Registered Dental Assistant Application along with the appropriate fee ($106.05).
26-2918319091.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2560983035.title: Dental Hygienist, Clinical/Nonclinical (R.D.H.)
26-2560983035.description: To receive a RDH Clinical/Nonclinical Limited License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must graduate from a CODA/ADA-accredited dental hygiene program, must be enrolled in a postgraduate educational program, and take and pass a fingerprint report and criminal background check. After meeting these requirements, the applicant must submit a license application along with the appropriate fee ($31.80).
26-2560983035.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2560983034.title: Dental Hygienist, Educational Limited (R.D.H.)
26-2560983034.description: To receive a RDH Educational Limited License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must graduate from a CODA/ADA-accredited dental hygiene program, must be enrolled in a postgraduate educational program, and take and pass a fingerprint report and criminal background check. After meeting these requirements, the applicant must submit a license application along with the appropriate fee ($31.80).
26-2560983034.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2912292021.title: Dental Hygienist, Registered (R.D.H.)
26-2912292021.description: To receive a Registered Dental Hygienist License, an applicant must graduate from a CODA/ADA-accredited dental assisting program, pass the National Board Dental Hygiene Examination and pass the ADEX Regional Dental Hygiene Examination. After meeting these requirements, the applicant must submit a Dental Hygienist License Application along with the appropriate fee ($47.70).
26-2912292021.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-4103483321.title: Dental Clinical/Nonclinical Limited
26-4103483321.description: To receive a Dental Clinical/Nonclinical Limited License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must graduate from a CODA/ADA-accredited dental school, must be appointed to a clinical or nonclinical academic faculty position, and take and pass a fingerprint report and criminal background check. After meeting these requirements, the applicant must submit a license application along with the appropriate fee ($53.00).
26-4103483321.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2597885846.title: Dental Educational Limited
26-2597885846.description: To receive a Dental Educational Limited License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must graduate from a CODA/ADA-accredited dental school, be enrolled in a postgraduate educational program, and take and pass a fingerprint report and criminal background check. After meeting these requirements, the applicant must submit a license application along with the appropriate fee ($53.00).
26-2597885846.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2900291021.title: Dentist (D.D.S.)
26-2900291021.description: To receive a Dentist License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must graduate from a CODA/ADA-accredited dental school, pass Parts 1 and 2 of the National Board Dental Examinations, and pass the ADEX Dental Examination (including the periodontal section). After meeting these requirements, the applicant must submit a Dentist License Application along with the appropriate fee ($127.25).
26-2900291021.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2921291029.title: Endodontist
26-2921291029.description: To receive an Endodontics License from the State of Michigan, an applicant must hold a current Michigan Dentist license, graduate from a CODA/ADA accredited dental specialty program, and pass the appropriate American Board written examination OR hold Diplomate status. Once these requirements have been met, an applicant must submit the Dental Specialty license application along with the appropriate fee ($47.70).
26-2921291029.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2924291029.title: Pediatric Dentist
26-2924291029.description: An applicant must graduate from a dental school that is in compliance with the standards of the Board, pass all parts of the national board examination and pass the combined regional examination in dentistry. The fee for this license is $127.25.
26-2924291029.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2925291029.title: Periodontist
26-2925291029.description: An applicant must graduate from a dental school that is in compliance with the standards of the Board, pass all parts of the national board examination and pass the combined regional examination in dentistry. The fee for this license is $127.25.
26-2925291029.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-7524334390.title: Certified Criminal Justice Professional?(C.C.J.P.)
26-7524334390.description: A certified criminal justice professional must complete 100 hours of education, 2,000 hours of criminal justice work experience, 100 hours of supervision, and pass the IC&RC CCJP (Supplemental) Examination. The fee for this license is $65.00.
26-7524334390.agency: Michigan Certification Board for Addiction Professionals

26-6781691430.title: Certified Electronic Operator (C.E.O.)
26-6781691430.description: To receive certification as a Certified Electronic Operator, an individual must have successfully completed the 4-week online CEO examination preparation course through Lansing Community College. Additionally, they must pass the CEO certification examination. Upon meeting these qualifications, an applicant must submit an application for certification.

26-4998918581.title: Certified Electronic Recorder (C.E.R.)
26-4998918581.description: To receive certification as a Certified Electronic Recorder, an individual must have successfully completed an approved course of study (either the Michigan Electronic Court Reporters Association CER Workshop, OR Lansing Community College's CER course). Additionally, they must pass the CER certification examination. Upon meeting these qualifications, an applicant must submit an application for certification.

26-7204472111.title: Electrical Apprentice
26-7204472111.description: To receive an Electrical Apprentice license in the State of Michigan, an applicant must submit an application online or mail the completed application and required documents to the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs. Additionally, they must remit the $15.00 application fee.
26-7204472111.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-7202472111.title: Electrical Contractor
26-7202472111.description: An applicant for an Electrical Contractor license must hold a Master Electrician License or have at least 1 master electrician residing in the State of Michigan who is in his or her full-time employ. Additionally, the applicant must take and pass the Electrical/Fire Alarm/Sign Contractor examination along with the $300.00 fee payable to PSI.
26-7202472111.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-7203472111.title: Electrician, Journeyperson
26-7203472111.description: An applicant for an Electrical Journeyman license must be at least 20 years old and must have at least 8,000 hours of practical experience over a period of at least 4 years that is related to electrical construction, maintenance of buildings, electrical wiring, or equipment. This experience must be under the direct supervision of a licensed person. Additionally, the applicant must take and pass the Journeyman examination and submit the $40.00 license fee.
26-7203472111.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-7201472111.title: Electrician, Master
26-7201472111.description: To receive a Master Electrician License, an applicant must be at least 22 years old, have held an Electrical Journeyman's license for at least 2 years, and have had at least 12,000 hours of practical experience over a period of at least 6 years that is related to electrical construction, maintenance of buildings, electrical wiring, or equipment. This experience must be under the direct supervision of a Master Electrician. Additionally, the applicant must take and pass the Master Electrician examination and submit the $50.00 license fee.
26-7201472111.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-7003474011.title: Inspector, Electrical
26-7003474011.description: To receive an Electrical Inspector registration, an applicant must have at least 2 years of experience as a licensed electrical journey worker OR should be licensed as a master electrician. Additionally, an applicant must complete the required number of hours of education in approved educational or training programs. Upon meeting these requirements, an application must be submitted to the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs along with the $25.00 application fee.
26-7003474011.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-7602474099.title: Sign Specialist
26-7602474099.description: A sign specialist must have at least 4,000 hours of experience, complete the approved training course and pass the examination. The fee for this license is $40.00.
26-7602474099.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-7302474021.title: Elevator Contractor
26-7302474021.description: To receive an Elevator Contractor's License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must have at least five years of experience as an elevator constructor, journeyperson, or equivalent, and must take and pass the examination.
26-7302474021.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-7006474011.title: Elevator Inspector
26-7006474011.description: To receive a General Elevator Inspector License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must have three years of experience in elevator construction (with at least one reference certifying the applicant's experience). Additionally, an applicant must also pass the written and oral examination.
26-7006474011.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-7301474021.title: Elevator Journeyperson
26-7301474021.description: To receive a General Journeyperson License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must have three years of continuous employment as a supervisor of elevator construction or service, OR as an elevator constructor, serviceman, maintenance man, or repairman. Additionally, an applicant must also pass the Journeyperson examination.
26-7301474021.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-3211292041.title: Emergency Medical Technician (E.M.T.)
26-3211292041.description: To receive an EMT license in the State of Michigan, an individual must be at least 18 years old, complete a Michigan EMT course within the last 2 years, and be nationally registered. Once these requirements have been met, an applicant must submit a license application online and remit the appropriate fees. Additionally, upon receiving a license, a recipient must accrue Michigan approved continuing education credits OR complete a Michigan approved refresher course.
26-3211292041.agency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services · Emergency Medical Services

26-3221292041.title: Emergency Medical Technician, Paramedic (E.M.T)
26-3221292041.description: To receive a Paramedic license in the State of Michigan, an individual must be at least 18 years old, complete a Michigan course within the last 2 years, and be nationally registered. Once these requirements have been met, an applicant must submit a license application online and remit the appropriate fees. Additionally, upon receiving a license, a recipient must accrue Michigan approved continuing education credits OR complete a Michigan approved refresher course.
26-3221292041.agency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services · Emergency Medical Services

26-3214292041.title: Emergency Medical Technician, Specialist (E.M.T.)
26-3214292041.description: To receive a Specialist license in the State of Michigan, an individual must be at least 18 years old, complete a Michigan course within the last 2 years, and be nationally registered. Once these requirements have been met, an applicant must submit a license application online and remit the appropriate fees. Additionally, upon receiving a license, a recipient must accrue Michigan approved continuing education credits OR complete a Michigan approved refresher course.
26-3214292041.agency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services · Emergency Medical Services

26-6700299011.title: Sanitarian, Registered
26-6700299011.description: A Sanitarian must hold the National Environmental Health Association (NEHA) Registered Environmental Health Specialist/Registered Sanitarian (REHS/RS) credential, or complete a bachelor's degree in an environmental health field and two years of work experience in an environmental health field, or complete a master's or doctoral degree in an environmental health related field and one year of work experience in an environmental health field. All candidates must pass the NEHA REHS/RS Examination and pay the fee of $80.80.
26-6700299011.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2710395094.title: Esthetician
26-2710395094.description: To receive an Esthetician license in Michigan, an applicant must be at least 17 years old, have attained the educational equivalent of 9th grade, and have completed at least 400 hours of training in a licensed cosmetology school OR performed a 6-month cosmetology apprenticeship. Upon meeting these requirements, they must pass the required theory and practical exam administered by PSI Services and submit a license application along with the appropriate application fee.
26-2710395094.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2722251194.title: Esthetician Instructor
26-2722251194.description: To receive an Esthetician Instructor License in Michigan, an applicant must have attained a high school diploma or its equivalent, have a current Michigan cosmetology license, and have at least 3 years of practical experience in natural hair cultivation, hair service, skin care services, and manicuring services (which includes 1 year in a cosmetology establishment). Finally, the applicant must have at least 500 hours of instructor training, and must pass the theory and practical examination administered by PSI Services. Upon completion of these requirements, an applicant can then submit an Instructor License application along with the appropriate fee ($63.50).
26-2722251194.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-3068647880.title: Esthetician Limited Instructor
26-3068647880.description: To receive an Esthetician Limited Instructor License in Michigan, an applicant must first have attained a high school diploma or its equivalent, have completed at least 300 hours of instructor training and have passed the theory and practical exam administered by PSI Services. Upon completion of these requirements, an applicant can then submit an Instructor License application along with the appropriate fee ($63.00).
26-3068647880.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2718395094.title: Esthetician, Apprentice
26-2718395094.description: To receive an Esthetician Apprentice License, an applicant must submit a registration application the Michigan Bureau of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs and remit the $25.00 application fee.
26-2718395094.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-8933132052.title: Investment Advisor
26-8933132052.description: The application for investment adviser registration is a two-part. It involves the electronic filing of Form ADV Part I, ADV Part 2, and other documents. The examination process varies depending on the complexity of the Applicant's business model. The fee for this application is $200.00.
26-8933132052.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Corporations, Securities & Commercial

00-FinOpL.title: Series 39 - Direct Participation Programs Limited Principal
00-FinOpL.description: Covered supervisory activities and products include regulatory compliance over sales of: ?Direct participation program limited partnerships (e.g., real estate, oil and gas, and equipment leasing) ?Limited liability companies ?S corporations In addition to sales supervision, the Series 39 qualifies a principal for the overall supervision of a firm’s investment banking and securities business—including compliance, underwriting and advertising—for those activities specially covered by each supervisory principal’s license.

26-8805251194.title: Fire Service Instructor
26-8805251194.description: In order for an applicant to receive a Fire Service Instructor certification, they must first become a probationary fire service instructor. A probationary instructor must have at least three years of fire service experience, be certified to the Fire Fighter 2 level, complete the MFFTC Instructor Orientation class and the MFFTC Educational Methodology OR Michigan Fire Instructor 1 course. Upon meeting these requirements, they must apply to become a probationary instructor. To proceed to a certified instructor, an applicant must additionally have at least five years of fire service experience, complete at least 12 hours of mentoring with a certified instructor 1, and be evaluated by a Bureau of Fire Services Region Coordinator.
26-8805251194.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Fire Services

26-6000194092.title: Forensic Polygraph Examiner Intern
26-6000194092.description: To become an intern, an applicant is required to have satisfied the educational requirement for a polygraph examiner's license, submit proof of enrollment in an approved polygraph school and submit an application with the required fee ($25.00).
26-6000194092.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Corporations, Securities & Commercial

26-6001294092.title: Forensic Polygraph Examiner, Private
26-6001294092.description: A polygraph examiner must be a graduate of an accredited bachelor's program with not less than 15 semester hours of academic credit in the social or behavioral sciences. Additionally, applicant for a polygraph examiners license is required to have completed an internship training program consisting of an academic component and a practical training component. The applicant will need to submit an application with the required fee ($100.00).
26-6001294092.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Corporations, Securities & Commercial

26-6001194092.title: Forensic Polygraph Examiner, Public
26-6001194092.description: A polygraph examiner must be a graduate of an accredited bachelor's program with not less than 15 semester hours of academic credit in the social or behavioral sciences. Additionally, applicant for a polygraph examiners license is required to have completed an internship training program consisting of an academic component and a practical training component. The applicant will need to submit an application with the required fee ($25.00).
26-6001194092.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Corporations, Securities & Commercial

26-8960419099.title: Solicitor, Professional
26-8960419099.description: A Professional Solicitor must be registered with the Department of Attorney General to work under a licensed Professional Fund Raiser entity.

26-4501119061.title: Funeral Director (Mortuary Science)
26-4501119061.description: To receive a Mortuary Science (Funeral Director) License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must have graduated from a three-year course in mortuary science at an accredited school. This includes completing at least 60 semester/90 quarter hours of non-remedial college courses (with at least a 2.00 grade point average), as well as completing at least one year of instruction at an accredited mortuary science program (with at least a 2.00 grade point average). Additionally, an applicant must serve as a resident trainee for at least one year under the supervision of a mortuary science license holder. Finally, an applicant must pass the National Arts and National Science examination (exam fee is $250 per section), pass the Michigan Mortuary Science examination ($56), and submit a license application along with the $100 application fee.
26-4501119061.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Corporations, Securities & Commercial

26-4500119061.title: Funeral Director (Mortuary Science) Resident Trainee
26-4500119061.description: A mortuary science trainee must be of good moral character, possess a high school diploma or its equivalent. The fee due at the time of the application is $45.00.
26-4500119061.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Corporations, Securities & Commercial

26-8502393010.title: Casino Employees Level 2
26-8502393010.description: An applicant for a Casino Level 2 License must first apply to the casino's or supplier's Human Resources Department, who must provide a written statement that the casino/supplier has hired or intends to hire the applicant. An application along with a $100 application fee must be submitted to the Michigan Gaming and Control Board. Finally, a background examination must be completed and a $100 license fee submitted.

26-7701474041.title: Asbestos Abatement Contractor/Supervisor
26-7701474041.description: To receive an Asbestos Abatement Contractor License, an applicant must have workers' compensations insurance, acquire Michigan/EPA-approved training, acquire accreditation from MIOSHA Asbestos program, complete the Asbestos Abatement Contractor License application, and remit the $200-$400 application fee. The fee schedule for accreditation is $50.00.
26-7701474041.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Occupational Safety & Health Administration

26-7703192041.title: Asbestos Abatement Project Designer
26-7703192041.description: To receive an Asbestos Abatement Project Designer License, an applicant must have had at least two years of experience in Asbestos-related work, OR have had at least five years of experience in school building operations and maintenance. Additionally, an applicant must receive Michigan or EPA-approved training and receive accreditation from MIOSHA Asbestos Program. The fee schedule for accreditation is $150.00.
26-7703192041.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Occupational Safety & Health Administration

26-7705474041.title: Asbestos Abatement Worker
26-7705474041.description: To receive an Asbestos Abatement Worker License, an applicant must receive Michigan or EPA-approved training and receive accreditation from MIOSHA Asbestos Program. The fee schedule for accreditation is $50.00.
26-7705474041.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Occupational Safety & Health Administration

26-7801474011.title: Lead Abatement Inspector
26-7801474011.description: To receive a Lead Abatement Inspector certification, an applicant must first have a high school diploma or equivalent level of education and taken and passed a lead training course from one of the approved providers. After meeting these requirements, a Certified Lead Professional application should be submitted to the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services along with the initial fee ($175 to $250). Finally, the state exam must be taken within 6 months of successfully passing the training course.
26-7801474011.agency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services · Lead Services

26-7802192041.title: Lead Abatement Project Designer
26-7802192041.description: To receive a Lead Abatement Project Designer certification, an applicant must first have either a Bachelor's degree in engineering, architecture, or related field, OR have at least 2 years of experience in a related field. An applicant must also have passed the Abatement Supervisor class. After meeting these requirements, a Certified Lead Professional application should be submitted to the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services along with the initial fee ($105 to $180). Finally, the state exam must be taken within 6 months of successfully passing the training course.
26-7802192041.agency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services · Lead Services

26-7804471011.title: Lead Abatement Supervisor
26-7804471011.description: To receive a Lead Abatement Supervisor certification, an applicant must first have at least 1 year of experience as a certified Abatement Worker or at least 2 years of experience in a related field. Additionally, an applicant must take and pass an approved lead training course. After meeting these requirements, a Certified Lead Professional application should be submitted to the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services along with the initial fee ($125 to $150). Finally, the state exam must be taken within 6 months of successfully passing the training course.
26-7804471011.agency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services · Lead Services

26-7805474041.title: Lead Abatement Worker
26-7805474041.description: To receive a Lead Abatement Worker certification, an applicant must take and pass an approved lead training course. After meeting this requirement, a Certified Lead Professional application should be submitted to the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services along with the initial fee ($115 to $125). Finally, the state exam must be taken within 6 months of successfully passing the training course.
26-7805474041.agency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services · Lead Services

26-4721291111.title: Nurse Midwife
26-4721291111.description: Nurses need to graduate from an approved education program and pass the NCLEX examination. To specialize, a nurse must hold an additional certification. The fee for renewing a nursing license is $123.60.
26-4721291111.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-4800119111.title: Nursing Home Administrator
