26-4800119111.description: Nursing home administrators must take an approved course of instructional training in Nursing Home Administration and pass the NHA and NSBL examinations. The fee for this license is $80.50, biennially.
26-4800119111.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Community and Health Systems

26-swn43.title: Licensed Bachelor Social Worker
26-swn43.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing - Licensing Division · Board of Social Work

26-swn41.title: Licensed Master Social Worker - Macro
26-swn41.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing - Licensing Division · Board of Social Work

26-swn40.title: Licensed Master Social Worker-Clinical
26-swn40.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing - Licensing Division · Board of Social Work

26-swn44.title: Limited Bachelor Social Worker
26-swn44.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing - Licensing Division · Board of Social Work

26-swn42.title: Limited License Master's Social Worker
26-swn42.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing - Licensing Division · Board of Social Work

26-3501414011.title: Hearing Aid Dealer
26-3501414011.description: To receive a Michigan Hearing Aid Dealer License, an applicant must be at least 18 years old, have completed at least two years of experience as a hearing aid salesperson under the direct supervision of a licensed hearing aid dealer, and must pass the Hearing Aid Dealer examination administered by PSI Services. The cost of the exam is $76.00. Upon meeting these requirements, the applicant must submit the Hearing Aid Dealer application along $180.00 application fee.
26-3501414011.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-3502419099.title: Hearing Aid Salesperson
26-3502419099.description: For an applicant to receive the Hearing Aid Salesperson License in the State of Michigan, they must be at least 18 years old, have completed at least six months as a trainee, and must pass the Hearing Aid Salesperson Examination ($72.00). Upon completion of these requirements, the applicant must then submit a license application along with the $120.00 application fee.
26-3502419099.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-3500419099.title: Hearing Aid Trainee
26-3500419099.description: To receive a Hearing Aid Trainee License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must submit a license application along with the $50.00 application fee.
26-3500419099.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-4600311012.title: Nurse Aide, Certified (C.N.A.)
26-4600311012.description: To become a CNA, new candidates must first complete a Michigan approved training course. Following successful completion of a training course, a candidate must apply to Prometric for testing and eligibility. The fee for this license is $115.00, renewed biennially.
26-4600311012.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Community and Health Systems

26-6102131071.title: Personnel Agent
26-6102131071.description: To receive a Employment Agent License, an applicant must pass the Personnel Agent examination administered through PSI Services. The exam fee is $56.00. Additionally, an applicant must submit the Consulting Agent License application and remit the $70.00 application fee.
26-6102131071.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-6820211093.title: Social Service Technician (S.S.T)
26-6820211093.description: Social Service Technician must have completed an Associate's degree in Social Work from a CSWE-accredited program, or be currently employed in social or human services and have either completed at least 2,000 hours of supervised social work experience over at least a one year period, or have completed at least two years of college in a regionally-accredited institution with at least four courses relevant to human service needs. The fee for this license is $42.40.
26-6820211093.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-8851493023.title: Mechanic, Master
26-8851493023.description: A person first must pass a test for each repair category in which certification is desired. Then you must complete an application for certification and return the application with the $25.00 fee to the Office of Investigative Services.

26-7103499021.title: Mechanical Contractor
26-7103499021.description: Mechanical contractors must have three years of experience and pass an exam before becoming licensed. The fee for this license is $300.00.
26-7103499021.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-8852493023.title: Motor Vehicle Specialty Mechanic
26-8852493023.description: A person first must pass a test for each repair category in which certification is desired. Then you must complete an application for certification and return the application with the $25.00 fee to the Office of Investigative Services.

00-Ins.title: NIPR Insurance Registry
00-Ins.description: Licensed Insurance Occupations must also be registered at the federal level.

26-4949264588.title: Vehicle Dealer Broker
26-4949264588.description: To receive a Vehicle Dealer-Broker license, an applicant must submit and complete a License Application, have Michigan no-fault insurance, have written verification of zoning and municipal approval, an established place of business, a surety bond, Michigan no-fault fleet insurance, and pay the appropriate license fee ($75-$160).

26-6300193031.title: Psychologist
26-6300193031.description: A psychologist must graduate from an approved doctoral program and complete an internship at least 2,000 hours as part of the doctoral degree program. In addition, a candidate must complete at least 2,000 hours of supervised post-degree psychology experience and pass the examination. The fee for this license is $159.05.
26-6300193031.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-6310193031.title: Psychologist, Masters Degree Limited
26-6310193031.description: To obtain a master's limited license in psychology, a candidate must complete at least 2,000 hours of supervised post-degree psychology experience and a 500 hour practicum. In addition, the candidate must pass an examination. The fee for this license is $127.25.
26-6310193031.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-3901171012.title: Landscape Architect, Licensed
26-3901171012.description: For an applicant to receive a Landscape Architect License from the State of Michigan, they must have completed an accredited bachelor's or master's program and completed three years of professional experience in the practice of landscape architecture (two years if a master's degree is possessed). Additionally, an applicant must establish a Council of Landscape Architects Registration Boards Council Record ($150.00 cost) and complete the Landscape Architecture Registration Examination ($1,780 cost for four-part exam). Upon completing these requirements, an applicant must then submit a license application along with the $260 license fee.
26-3901171012.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-8811231011.title: Attorney
26-8811231011.description: To receive an Attorney's License in Michigan, an applicant must be admitted to the State Bar.

26-8921132072.title: Loan Originator, Mortgage
26-8921132072.description: To receive a Loan Originator License, an applicant must have completed at least three hours of federal law and regulations, three hours of ethics (including instruction on fraud, consumer protection, and fair lending issues), two hours of training related to lending standards for nontraditional mortgage product markets, and twelve hours of undefined instruction on mortgage origination. This pre-licensure education must include 2 hours of Michigan content. Upon completion of these requirements, an applicant must then either pass both the National and Michigan State components of the SAFE test, OR pass the National and stand-alone UST components of the SAFE Test, OR pass the National Test Components with Uniform State Content. Finally, the applicant must submit a license application to the NMLS. License fees include a $30.00 initial processing fee, $250.00 license/registration fee, $15 for a credit report, and $36.25 for an FBI criminal background check.
26-8921132072.agency: Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services

26-4700292061.title: Nurse, Licensed Practical (L.P.N.)
26-4700292061.description: Nurses need to graduate from an approved education program and pass the NCLEX examination. To specialize, a nurse must hold an additional certification. The fee for renewing a nursing license is $123.60.
26-4700292061.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2712395092.title: Manicurist
26-2712395092.description: A manicurist must complete not less than 400 hours of training in a licensed school of cosmetology or perform a 6-month apprenticeship program within a licensed cosmetology establishment. A manicurist must pass the required theory and practical examination administered by PSI Services, LLC (PSI). Licenses expire biennially, the renewal fee is $48.00.
26-2712395092.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2721251194.title: Manicurist Instructor
26-2721251194.description: A manicurist instructor must hold a current Michigan license, have at least 3 years of practical experience, and completed 300 hours of instructor training. Licenses expire biennially, the renewal fee is $48.00.
26-2721251194.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-3899784351.title: Manicurist Limited Instructor
26-3899784351.description: To receive a Manicurist Limited Instructor License in Michigan, an applicant must first have attained a high school diploma or its equivalent, have completed at least 300 hours of instructor training and have passed the theory and practical exam administered by PSI Services. Upon completion of these requirements, an applicant can then submit an Instructor License application along with the appropriate fee ($63.00).
26-3899784351.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2719395092.title: Manicurist, Apprentice
26-2719395092.description: An apprentice must be under the supervision of a license holder and pay the registration of $25.00.
26-2719395092.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-1510112011.title: Promoter
26-1510112011.description: All individuals involved in Unarmed Combat Contests where an admission fee is charged or prizes are granted, should be licensed by the Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs. The fee to renew a license is $300.00, which must be paid annually.
26-1510112011.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Corporations, Securities & Commercial

26-6400211019.title: Counselor, Licensed Professional
26-6400211019.description: To receive a Professional Counselor License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must have received a master's or doctoral degree in counseling and have completed at least 48 semester hours or 72 quarter hours in counseling topics. Additionally, those with a master's degree are required to accrue at least 3,000 hours of post-degree counseling experience within a 2-year period, with 100 hours gained in the direct presence of a supervisor. Less is required for those studying counseling beyond a master's degree. Finally, after passing the National Counselor Examination, an individual may submit a license application along with the appropriate application fee ($84.80 to $121.90).
26-6400211019.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-6403211019.title: Counselor, Limited Licensed Professional
26-6403211019.description: To receive a Limited Professional Counselor License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must have received a master's or doctoral degree in counseling and have completed at least 48 semester hours or 72 quarter hours in counseling topics. Finally, an individual may submit a license application along with the appropriate application fee ($84.80 to $121.90).
26-6403211019.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-4100211013.title: Marriage & Family Therapist
26-4100211013.description: A marriage and family therapist needs to be a graduate from an accredited educational program. A licensee then needs to complete at least 1,000 hours direct client contact that supervised by a licensed MFT. After passing the National Marital and Family Therapy Examination, a licensee must pay the $85.85 fee.
26-4100211013.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-3100319011.title: Massage Therapist
26-3100319011.description: Massage therapy licensees must graduate from an approved massage therapy supervised curriculum and pass a national certification exam. The license fee is $100.75.
26-3100319011.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

00-52.title: Assistant Engineer (Limited - Oceans)
00-52.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as an Assistant Engineer (Limited - Oceans) include 1,080 days at sea, with 540 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-52.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-47.title: First Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-47.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a First Assistant Engineer - Upper Level, the applicant must complete 360 days of service as a Second or Third Assistant Engineer; while holding a Second Assistant Engineer license. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations
00-47.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-49.title: Third Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-49.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Third Assistant Engineer (upper Level, the applicant must complete one of the following: 1080 days of service in the engine room with 720 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED); or 1080 days as a machinist apprentice engaged in construction or repair of marine, locomotive, or stationary engines plus 360 days of sea service in an engine room as oiler, watertender, or jr. engineer; or graduate from an approved course of studies. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-49.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

26-4400291126.title: Respiratory Therapist
26-4400291126.description: Respiratory Therapists must obtain a degree from an accredited program and pass the national examination. The fee for this license is $100.75.
26-4400291126.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

00-10.title: Nuclear Facility Operator
00-10.description: Nuclear Facility Operators are required to have either training or experience to become licensed. They must pass a medical exam, a written test, and an operating test. Although the license is granted for 6 years, licensees must pass another medical exam every two years and an operating test annually. Also, they must undergo requalification training while employed. Nuclear Facility Senior Operators have additional experience and pass another exam to be promoted from Nuclear Facility Operators. Further information can be found at the web site: http://www.nrc.gov/reactors/operator-licensing.html

26-4720291111.title: Nurse Anesthetist
26-4720291111.description: Nurses need to graduate from an approved education program and pass the NCLEX examination. To specialize, a nurse must hold an additional certification. The fee for renewing a nursing license is $123.60.
26-4720291111.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-4722291111.title: Nurse Practitioner
26-4722291111.description: Nurses need to graduate from an approved education program and pass the NCLEX examination. To specialize, a nurse must hold an additional certification. The fee for renewing a nursing license is $123.60.
26-4722291111.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

00-63.title: Hospital Corpsman
00-63.description: A Hospital Corpsman is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A hospital corpsman must have U.S. military experience as and a rating of hospital corpsman or Health Services Technician or equivalent. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-63.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

26-2633674001.title: Certified Prevention Consultant?(C.P.C.)
26-2633674001.description: A certified prevention consultant must have 8,000 hours of experience, 240 hours of education, 240 hours of supervision and pass the IC&RC/PS, Prevention Specialist examination. The fee for this license is $65.00.
26-2633674001.agency: Michigan Certification Board for Addiction Professionals

26-2370780615.title: Certified Prevention Specialist?(C.P.S.)
26-2370780615.description: A certified prevention specialist must have 2,000 hours of experience, 120 hours of education, 120 hours of supervision and pass the IC&RC/PS, Prevention Specialist examination. The fee for this license is $65.00.
26-2370780615.agency: Michigan Certification Board for Addiction Professionals

26-5200291122.title: Occupational Therapist
26-5200291122.description: Occupational therapists must be graduates from an accredited program and pass both the certification examination and the jurisprudence examination. The fee for this license is $100.75.
26-5200291122.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-4900291041.title: Optometrist
26-4900291041.description: An optometrist needs to be a graduate of an accredited program. In addition, optometrists need to pass the jurisprudence exam and parts I, II, and III of the National Board of Examiners in Optometry (NBEO) examination as well as the Treatment and Management of Ocular Disease (TMOD) examination embedded in part II. The fee for this license is $127.25, biennially.
26-4900291041.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2922291022.title: Oral Maxillofacial Surgeon
26-2922291022.description: An applicant must graduate from a dental school that is in compliance with the standards of the Board, pass all parts of the national board examination and pass the combined regional examination in dentistry. The fee for this license is $127.25.
26-2922291022.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2923291023.title: Orthodontist
26-2923291023.description: An applicant must graduate from a dental school that is in compliance with the standards of the Board, pass all parts of the national board examination and pass the combined regional examination in dentistry. The fee for this license is $127.25.
26-2923291023.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-2920291024.title: Prosthodontist
26-2920291024.description: An applicant must graduate from a dental school that is in compliance with the standards of the Board, pass all parts of the national board examination and pass the combined regional examination in dentistry. The fee for this license is $127.25.
26-2920291024.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-5210312011.title: Occupational Therapy Assistant
26-5210312011.description: Occupational therapists assistants must be graduates from an accredited program and pass both the certification examination and the jurisprudence examination. The fee for this license is $100.75.

26-8853112022.title: Salvage Vehicle Agent
26-8853112022.description: Salvage Vehicle Agents may buy or sell distressed vehicles, scrap vehicles, or component parts at auctions or salvage pools in Michigan. They are licensed by the Secretary of State.

26-5302291051.title: Pharmacist
26-5302291051.description: Pharmacists must graduate from an accredited program, complete at least 1,600 hours internship experience, and pass the NAPLEX and jurisprudence examinations. The fee for this license is $60.60.

26-5304291051.title: Pharmacist, Educational Limited

26-2986708890.title: Pharmacy Technician
26-2986708890.description: To receive a Pharmacy Technician license in the State of Michigan, an applicant must have obtained a high school diploma or equivalent and pass the certified pharmacy technician exam. Additionally, an applicant must submit the Pharmacy Technician License application along with the $55.55 licensing fee to the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs. Finally, a fingerprint report and criminal background check must be completed.

26-5500291123.title: Physical Therapist
26-5500291123.description: Physical therapists need to be a graduate of an accredited program and pass the national exam. The fee for this license is $116.65.
26-5500291123.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

00-80.title: Marine Physician Assistant
00-80.description: A Marine Physician Assistant is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A physician assistant must also have training as a physician's assistant or nurse practitioner. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-80.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

26-5600291071.title: Physician's Assistant
26-5600291071.description: A physician's assistant is licensed by the Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs to examine, diagnose, and treat patients under a licensed physician.
26-5600291071.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

00-31.title: Tankerman
00-31.description: Tankerman refers to several endorsements or qualified ratings to Merchant Marine Documents (MMD). All Tankerman endorsements require qualifying experience, training in firefighting and cargo (dangerous liquids or liquefied gasses), and passing an exam. Endorsements include Tankerman - Person-In-Charge (Tankerman PIC), Tankerman-Engineer, Tankerman Assistant, and Tankerman - PIC (Barge). Tankerman endorsements are valid for the duration of the MMD, which is issued for 5 years. Renewal of certification requires meeting all the requirements to renew the MMD and either have recent qualifying experience or training. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR13.109) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr13_02.html.
00-31.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

26-7101472011.title: Boiler Installer
26-7101472011.description: To receive a Boiler Installer License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must apply for the exam and remit the $80.00 application fee to the Michigan Bureau of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs. An applicant must then take and pass the exam.
26-7101472011.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-7102472011.title: Boiler Repairer
26-7102472011.description: To receive a Boiler Repairer's License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must apply for the exam and remit the $80.00 application fee to the Michigan Bureau of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs. An applicant must then take and pass the exam.
26-7102472011.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-7005474011.title: Inspector, Plumbing
26-7005474011.description: To receive a Plumbing Inspector registration, an applicant must first have possessed a journey license for at least 2 years OR should be licensed as a master plumber. Additionally, an applicant must complete the required number of hours of education in approved educational or training programs. Upon meeting these requirements, an application must be submitted to the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs along with the $25.00 application fee.
26-7005474011.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-7402472152.title: Plumber, Journeyperson
26-7402472152.description: A journey plumber must have more than 6000 hours experience attained over a period of not less than 3 years as a registered plumbing?apprentice in the practical installation of plumbing under the supervision of a licensed authorized master plumber. In addition, they must also pass an exam. The fee for this license is $40.00.
26-7402472152.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-7401472152.title: Plumber, Master
26-7401472152.description: A master plumber must have 4,000 hours experience in work as a journey plumber over a period of not less than 2 years immediately preceding the date of the application. They must also pass an exam. The fee for this application is $300.00.
26-7401472152.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Construction Codes

26-8412474071.title: Septage Hauler
26-8412474071.description: Septage Haulers need a license provided by the Department of Environmental Quality to remove and transport septage waste for disposal. The fee for this license is $200.00.

26-8302475021.title: Water Well Contractor
26-8302475021.description: A Well Drilling Contractor must have at least two years of experience, provide records of 20 water wells and pumps installed, provide references, and pass the examination offered by the Department of Environmental Quality. The fee for this license is $40.00.

26-5900291081.title: Podiatrist
26-5900291081.description: A Podiatrist must be a graduate of an approved program. In addition, they must pass parts I, II, and III of the examination developed and scored by the National Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners and the jurisprudence exam. The fee for this license is $127.25.
26-5900291081.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-5903291081.title: Podiatrist, Educational Limited
26-5903291081.description: An intern in postgraduate podiatric study with a hospital, clinic, or preceptorship program must obtain a limited license. The fee for this license is $143.15.
26-5903291081.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-8950273031.title: Lobbyist Agent
26-8950273031.description: A Lobbyist Agent is a person that receives compensation in excess of $475.00 dollars for lobbying on behalf of employers during any 12 month period. A lobbyist agent must comply with all Michigan Campaign Finance and Election Laws.

26-5250866531.title: EBL Investigator
26-5250866531.description: A EBL Investigator must first become a lead inspector and risk assessor. There is no fee for this license.

26-8804339021.title: Professional Investigator
26-8804339021.description: A professional investigator must be a graduate from an accredited program and post a bond or insurance policy for $10,000.00. The initial fee for this license is $750.00 with a $300.00 renewal fee.

26-8803211092.title: Parole/Probation Agent, State
26-8803211092.description: The new field agent and field service assistants training program consists of four (4) phases encompassing three weeks of classroom training and seven weeks of on-the-job training. Phase IV is initial handgun training for new field agents and field service assistants who elect to carry a handgun.

00-05.title: Customs Broker
00-05.description: Customs brokers must pass an exam to obtain a license. Further information can be found at the US Customs Service web site: http://www.customs.gov/xp/cgov/import/broker_management/.

00-59.title: Purser
00-59.description: The Purser, one of a ship's staff officers, is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A Junior Assistant Purser requires no experience. A Senior Assistant Purser requires 180 days, a Purser requires 360 days, and a Chief Purser requires 720 days of service aboard vessels while performing duties related to the purser's office. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.

26-5508312021.title: Physical Therapist Assistant

26-6502419021.title: Real Estate Broker, Associate

26-6502419021.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

26-6503419021.title: Real Estate Broker, Individual
26-6503419021.description: An individual real estate broker must complete 90 hours of approved prelicensure education, complete 3 years of experience, and pass an examination. The fee for this license is $143.00.
26-6503419021.agency: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs · Bureau of Professional Licensing

00-61.title: Professional Nurse
00-61.description: A ship's Professional Nurse is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A professional nurse must also hold a valid license as a registered nurse issued within the United States. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.

26-4710291111.title: Nurse, Registered (R.N.)
26-4710291111.description: Nurses need to graduate from an approved education program and pass the NCLEX examination. To specialize, a nurse must hold an additional certification. The fee for renewing a nursing license is $123.60.

26-8711291111.description: Nurses need to graduate from an approved education program and pass the NCLEX examination. To specialize, a nurse must hold an additional certification. The fee for renewing a nursing license is $123.60.

00-03.title: Able Seaman - AB
00-03.description: Requirements for an Able Seaman license include a medical certificate of excellent health, and a certificate attesting to vision, color perception, and general physical condition. While no experience or formal schooling is required, training at a union-operated school is the best source. With experience at sea, and perhaps union-sponsored training, an ordinary seaman with a Merchant Marine Document (MMD) can pass the Able Seaman exam and move up with 3 years of service. Please see the U.S. Coast Guard web site at: http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, the Veteran's Employment and Training Service (VETS) web site at http://umet-vets.dol.gov/ableseaman.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html
00-03.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-30.title: Lifeboatman - LBMAN
00-30.description: A person with a Merchant Marine Document (MMD) with one year of experience at sea in the deck department, two years experience in any other department on vessels greater than 100 gross tons, or who has completed a USCG approved course and 3 months of sea experience may take written and practical exams to be endorsed with the qualified rating of Lifeboatman (LB). An MMD with a qualified rating is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through documented recent experience, pass an exam, or complete a training course. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR12.10-7) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-30.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-33.title: Merchant Mariner's Document - MMD
00-33.description: The United States Coast Guard issues a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) to unlicensed personnel who support the operation of a vessel. Unqualified ratings are issued to entry level individuals who typically have little or no sea service for the following rating types: ordinary seaman (deck department), wiper (engineering department), or food handler (steward's department). Qualified ratings are issued based on previous sea service in a particular department or specialized training. Qualified ratings for members in the deck department are issued by rating type (e.g. Able Seaman) and vessel type restrictions (e.g. sail vessels or offshore supply vessels). Qualified ratings for members in the engineering department are issued by type (e.g. Qualified Member of the Engine Department) and specific rating (e.g. oiler, fireman/watertender, junior engineer, deck engine mechanic, or engineman). Other ratings are issued for specialized training or experience, such as Lifeboatman, Tankerman, or GMDSS At-Sea Maintainer. An MMD is valid for 5 years and may be renewed. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-33.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-04.title: Ordinary Seaman
00-04.description: An Ordinary Seaman is a person holding a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) issued by the United States Coast Guard without qualified ratings. This is an entry level MMD and does not require maritime experience or a physical examination, but will require proof that the applicant has passed a chemical test for dangerous drugs. While no training is required, a union-operated school can provide useful background knowledge. An MMD is valid for 5 years and may be renewed. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-04.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-32.title: Qualified Member of the Engine Department - QMED
00-32.description: Qualified Member of the Engine Department - QMED A person with a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) having at least 6 months of underway service working as a wiper or coal passer in the engineering department may take a written exam and at least one rating exam (Fireman/Watertender, Oiler, Deck Engineer, Junior Engineer, Refrigeration Engineer, Electrician, Machinist, or Pumpman) to be endorsed as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Additional experience is required for some endorsements. Renewal of certification requires meeting all the requirements to renew the MMD and either have recent qualifying experience or training. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.15-11) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-32.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

26-8703211012.description: School Counselors must complete at least 30 graduate level semester hours in an approved school counselor education program, complete at least 600 hours of internship, and pass the Michigan Certification Examination. The fee for this license is $160.00.

26-8843253099.title: Driver Education Instructor
26-8843253099.description: To receive a Driver Education Instructor certification, an applicant must be at least 21 years old, have a valid driver license, and must have taken at least 8 semester hours of driver education instructor preparation courses. 00-28.title: Ocean Transportation Intermediary - OTI
00-28.description: Licensure as an Ocean Transportation Intermediary (OTI) - Ocean Freight Forwarder requires that the designated employee for the company have three years of qualifying experience, meet character requirements, and be bonded. The license is issued indefinitely or until revoked or suspended. Details can be found at the FMC web sites http://www.fmc.gov/cfr/515.htm, http://www.fmc.gov/Help/OTI.htm, and the Code of Federal Regulations (46CFR515) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr515_02.html.

00-29.title: Ocean Transportation Intermediary -NVOCC
00-29.description: Licensure as an Ocean Transportation Intermediary (OTI)- Non-Vessel-Operating Common Carrier (NVOCC) requires that the qualifying individual for the company have three years of qualifying experience, meet character requirements, and be bonded. The license is issued indefinitely or until revoked or suspended. 00-67.title: Barge Supervisor
00-67.description: A Barge Supervisor is required to pass an exam, have 3 years of related work experience or an approved degree in engineering or engineering technology, plus at least 168 days of related experience. Specialized training is also required in stability of the mobile offshore drilling unit (ODU), survival at sea, and firefighting. Federal regulations can be found at the web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-67.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-37.title: Chief Mate - Upper Level
00-37.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Mate - Upper Level requires 360 days service as Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch (OIC) on Any Gross Tons oceangoing steam or motor vessels while licensed as a Second Mate. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. More information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-37.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-34.title: Deck Officers
00-34.description: The navigation of a vessel and management of the deck department is the responsibility of the Deck Officers. Deck officers' licenses are issued by grade (e.g., Master, Chief Mate, Second Mate, Third Mate, Mate and Operator), any vessel type restrictions (e.g. Uninspected Fishing Industry or Uninspected Passenger vessels), means of propulsion (Steam, Motor, Sail or Auxiliary Sail), vessel tonnage (from not more than 5 to any gross register tons), and route (e.g., Inland, Great Lakes, Near Coastal or Oceans). Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-34.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-40.title: Master - Lower Level
00-40.description: Obtaining a United States Coast Guard license as a Master - Lower Level requires a specified amount of qualifying service based on details such as vessel size and area of operation (ocean, near coastal, Great Lakes, or inland). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Detailed information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-40.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-36.title: Master - Upper Level
00-36.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Master - Upper Level requires 360 days service as Chief Mate on ocean Any Gross Tons steam or motor vessels; or 180 days as Chief Mate plus 360 days as Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch (OIC). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Detailed information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-36.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-66.title: Offshore Installation Manager - OIM
00-66.description: An Offshore Installation Manager (OIM) requires passing an exam and four years of related work experience or an approved degree in engineering or engineering technology and at least 168 days of related work experience. Specialized training in rig stability, oil well control or operation, firefighting and survival at sea are required. OIMs apply for an OIM Unrestricted License or one of four specialized licenses: OIM Surface Units on Location, OIM Surface Units Underway, OIM Bottom Bearing Units Underway, and OIM Bottom-Bearing Units on Location. Federal regulations can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SECTION=470&YEAR=1999&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-66.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-44.title: Pilot (Ship)
00-44.description: A license or endorsement as a Pilot is route-specific and requires experience navigating the body of water specified. A written exam and physical exam are also required. Further information on Pilot requirements can be found on the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/CFR-2002-title46-vol1/CFR-2002-title46-vol1-part10.
00-44.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-69.title: Radar Observer
00-69.description: The Radar Observer certificate is issued by the United States Coast Guard to licensed deck officers. It requires specialized training and examination in radar navigation and is issued for 5 years. Further information can be found in the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10.305) at web site http://frwebgate4.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/waisgate.cgi?WAISdocID=50176913269+4+2+0&WAISaction=retrieve and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-69.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-39.title: Third Mate - Upper Level
00-39.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Third Mate - Upper Level requires 1080 days service in the deck department of ocean steam or motor vessels with 6 months as Able Seaman (AB); or graduate from an approved marine academy; or completion of an approved 3 year apprentice mate training program; or 360 days as Master on ocean steam or motor vessels greater than 200 GT while licensed as a Master 1600 Gross Tons. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. More information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-39.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

26-7774077879.title: Sport Trolling (Charter Captains)
26-7774077879.description: An individual interest in sport trolling must submit an application with a $16.00 fee to the Department of Natural Resources.

00-68.title: Ballast Control Operator
00-68.description: A United States Coast Guard Ballast Control Operator is required to pass an exam and to have 1 year related experience, including at least 28 days as a trainee under a licensed Ballast Control Operator or a degree in engineering or engineering technology and at least 28 days as a trainee. Specialized training is also required in stability of the mobile offshore drilling unit (ODU), survival at sea, and firefighting. Federal regulations can be found at the web site http://frwebgate2.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/waisgate.cgi?WAISdocID=051618583+1+0+0&WAISaction=retrieve, http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-68.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-46.title: Chief Engineer
00-46.description: To be licensed by the United States Coast Guard as a Chief Engineer, the applicant must complete 360 days of service as a First Assistant Engineer; or while holding a First Assistant Engineer license, complete 360 days of service as follows: a minimum of 180 days of service as a First Assistant Engineer plus a minimum of 360 days as a Second or Third Assistant Engineer, Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-46.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-51.title: Chief Engineer (Limited - Near Coastal)
00-51.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Engineer (Limited - Near Coastal) include 1,440 days at sea, with 360 days as a Licensed Engineer & 720 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-51.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-50.title: Chief Engineer (Limited - Oceans)
00-50.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Engineer (Limited - Oceans), include 1,800 days at sea, with 720 days as a Licensed Engineer & 900 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-50.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-53.title: Designated Duty Engineer
00-53.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Designated Duty Engineer include specified service time at sea, with experience as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED) on a vessel of specified horsepower. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-53.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-45.title: Engineering Officers
00-45.description: The propulsion plant of a vessel and management of the engineering department is the responsibility of the Engineering Officers. Engineering officers' licenses are issued by grade (e.g., Chief Engineer, First Assistant Engineer, Second Assistant Engineer, Third Assistant Engineer, Assistant Engineer and Designated Duty Engineer), any vessel type restrictions (e.g. Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels or Uninspected Passenger vessels), means of propulsion (Steam or Motor), horsepower (from 1,000 to any horsepower), and route (e.g., Near Coastal or Oceans). License limitations for deck and engineering officers, including tonnage and horsepower, are based on the type of experience of each applicant and the passing of applicable written examinations. Each license has separate general, service and examination requirements. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-45.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

26-2926291029.title: Pathologist, Oral
26-2926291029.description: An applicant must graduate from a dental school that is in compliance with the standards of the Board, pass all parts of the national board examination and pass the combined regional examination in dentistry. The fee for this license is $127.25.

00-64.title: Enrolled Agent - EA
00-64.description: Requirements to become an enrolled agent of the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) are one of the following (1) pass an exam; or (2) document 5 years of relevant experience as an employee for the IRS. Continuing professional education hours every three-year cycle is required for renewal of the credential. Further information can be found at the IRS web site: http://www.irs.gov/taxpros/agents/index.html.
00-64.agency: Internal Revenue Service · Enrolled Practitioner Program Unit

26-3213253099.title: Emergency Medical Technician, Instructor/Coordinator (E.M.T.)
26-3213253099.description: To receive an EMT Instructor/Coordinator license in the State of Michigan, an individual must have completed a Michigan Instructor-Coordinator course within the prior two years, have three years of field experience providing direct patient care with a licensed Life Support Agency, and must be currently licensed as an EMT in Michigan at or above the level being applied for. Finally, an applicant must take the Instructor Coordinator exam via the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services. Once these requirements have been met, an applicant must submit a license application online and remit the appropriate fees.
26-3213253099.agency: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services · Emergency Medical Services

00-79.title: Aircraft Dispatcher
00-79.description: An Aircraft Dispatcher certificate requires that the individual has work experience as an aircraft dispatcher or related occupation such as pilot. Training in aircraft dispatching and passing written and practical tests are also required. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web site http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.51-65.70, and http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ

26-8841533032.title: Commercial Driver License (C.D.L.)
26-8841533032.description: An applicant for a Commercial Driver License must pass medical and driver qualifications, the required knowledge and vision tests, and a skills test through an approved third-party tester. The CDL fee is $25.00, with a $25.00 renewal fee.

26-6910292056.title: Veterinary Technician
26-6910292056.description: Veterinary Technicians must graduate from an accredited educational program and pass the Veterinary Technician Licensing Examination. The fee for this license is $41.00.

26-6900291131.title: Veterinarian

26-8303518031.title: Drinking Water Operator (Distribution System)
26-8303518031.description: To receive a Drinking Water Operator certification, an applicant must meet the education and experience requirements, submit a license application ($95) and take the Drinking Water Exam ($45.00-$75.00 per exam).

26-8414518031.title: Municipal Wastewater Treatment Plant Operator
26-8414518031.description: Municipal wastewater treatment plant operators need approved college credits and a certification examination to be licensed. The renewal fee is $95.00, annually.

26-8411518031.title: Storm Water Operator
26-8411518031.description: Storm Water Operators must pass an exam offered by the Department of Environmental Quality. The fee for this license is $95.00.

26-8413518031.title: Wastewater Treatment Plant Operator
26-8413518031.description: To receive an Industrial/Commercial Wastewater Treatment Plant Operator License in the State of Michigan, an applicant must have completed 6 months of operational experience in each unit process, the ability to read and write, comprehension of the principles and problems of management of the treatment process and facilities, the ability to perform arithmetic calculations to operate the waste treatment or control, and the ability to prepare the required report to the Department. Additionally, Level 3 requires the equivalent of 2 years of college education in engineering, chemistry, biological sciences, or an allied field, as well as 4 courses of post-high school level chemistry of biological sciences. Once these requirements have been met, an applicant must take and pass the exam for each unit process applied for.

26-8301533032.title: Water Hauler
26-8301533032.description: A Water Hauler must have an evaluation of the water hauling transportation tanks and equipment, approval of the water source facilities, knowledge of the use of chlorine for disinfection of water.
